text:
Alex: quick thought — what if we try a header-first prefetch for safetensors shards so we can mmmap the big blobs without fetching full manifest upfront?
Mona: can you sketch the handshake? curious how this differs from index-first approach we've debated.
Alex: idea: on open we do a tiny range request for 0..8k to grab shard header + per-tensor offsets. If header indicates compressed or chunked, fall back to full manifest fetch. Otherwise we mmmap and lazy-resolve ranges.
Tariq: that reduces roundtrips for most shards. but how do we ensure compatibility with multi-file shards (safetensors + sidecar index)?
Alex: sidecar index stays optional. header must include a compact index blob (offsets+checksum) embedded. sidecar only used when header flag says "index_missing".
Jen: hmm embedding index in header makes headers big. Do we have size/latency tradeoffs? 8k might be too small for some quantized bundles.
Alex: true. propose adaptive: request 4k; if header.magic indicates "idx_more", do a second range 4k-32k. worst-case two RTTs but usually 1.
Samir: what about resilience when caches evict parts? we rely on range support from stores (S3/GS). Not all CDNs upstream honor multiple small ranges.
Mona: plus need checksum/version to detect incompatible inline index format. We should include a format_version and index_format fields in header.
Tariq: operationally, how do we expose this to runtime? loader API needs a bool: allow_header_indexing (default true). Also expose diagnostics: header_fetch_time, fallback_count.
Alex: agreed. API sketch: load_shard(path, options={allow_header_indexing: true, prefetch_policy: "header-first"})
Jen: concern: tooling that writes safetensors needs to include tiny index. How painful to change exporters?
Samir: we can provide a shim in the weight packaging CLI to append index if missing. Also the runtime can fall back to manifest fetch if header absent — non-breaking.
Alex: good. Another point: memory mapping with file-descriptor passing for private deployments — we can mmmap after warmup thread prefetches index and first token ranges, then hand FD to worker. Reduces copy.
Mona: fd passing across containers only works on same host/VM. for Dedicated/Hosted we need a gRPC fetch path. make sure we don't couple API surface to FD. keep that an optimization for Private.
Tariq: warmup: propose two-stage warmup: stage 1 header-only to register tensors in cache metadata; stage 2 optimistic prefetch for first_kb_of_biggest_tensors if request pattern suggests low-latency path.
Jen: how do we pick first_kb? static (128KB) or dynamic based on seq_len? maybe dynamic, proportional to expected kv cache growth.
Samir: add heuristics: if model is chatty and typical prompt len < 512, prefetch first 256KB for attention weights, else 512KB. We can tune with telemetry.
Alex: deploy-bot: cpu-bench-v2 finished on staging.
build-bot: [deploy-bot] Found 3 build artifacts for header-prefetch prototype. Tests 12/14 passing.
Mona: for safety, logging: emit a compact header_index schema and a warning if inline index size > 16KB. can auto-tag bundles for repackage.
Tariq: compatibility layers: runtime should accept both: (a) full manifest, (b) header-inline-index, (c) manifest-sidecar. unify resolution to a ShardIndex interface. keep concrete formats behind adapters.
Jen: for evals, add regression checks: model logits unchanged when using header-first vs manifest-first. small numerical diffs expected but no quality regressions.
Alex: next steps: I'll prototype header encoder in packer, add loader flag, and a small benchmark (latency p95 on mmapped cold-start). Planning to spike this week.
Mona: +1. please include a short RFC blurb summarizing format fields and failure modes.
Samir: can we also add a fallback policy: if range requests > N fail, switch to single-shot full fetch to avoid tail latency.
Alex: good call — set N=2 by default.
Jen: thanks all. I'll mock exporter changes and test with a small quantized model.
Tariq: tagging infra: @mona @jen if we need any CDN headers toggles.
Alex: thanks everyone. will post prototype thread when ready.
